steps.label: Workspaces
steps.sub: one config, shared backend and credentials, low overhead

steps.label: Separate state files
steps.sub: one directory per env, own backend, real isolation

steps.label: The real question
steps.sub: do your environments need different people, not just different sizes?

code:
envs/
  dev/
    backend.tf   # key = "dev/network.tfstate"
    main.tf      # module "network" { source = "../../modules/network" }
  prod/
    backend.tf   # key = "prod/network.tfstate", own storage account
    main.tf      # module "network" { source = "../../modules/network" }
caption: Same shared module, but prod's state lives in its own storage account with its own access policy.
A different storage account means different Azure RBAC role assignments than dev's backend.

subtitle: dev.tfvars and prod.tfvars — the same module, sized completely differently.
